subdivision.heading: Additional Rules Specific to Originating Applications for Judicial Review

operative_text.controlling:
3.23(1)  The Court may stay the operation of a decision or act
sought to be set aside under an originating application for judicial
review pending final determination of the originating application.
(2)  Despite subrule (1), no order to stay is to be made if, in the
Court’s opinion, the stay would be detrimental either to the public
interest or to public safety.

BOOK_B.title: Stay of decision

commentary.text: Rule 3.23 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.23. 1. Jurisdiction to grant a stay In Société Culturelle Mamowapik v. Alberta (Gaming & Liquor Commission), 2000 ABCA 148, 2000 CarswellAlta 485, 261 A.R. 198, 83 Alta. L.R. (3d) 266, the applicant had its bingo licence revoked by the Commission. The applicant sought a stay of the Commission's order pending the hearing of a judicial review application. The learned Chambers judge in the Court of Queen's Bench refused to grant a stay. The applicant then sought an order from Russell, J.A., sitting alone, reversing the Chambers decision. In concluding that she did not have jurisdiction, her Ladyship said, at pp. 267-268: The applicants rely on Rule 753.15(1) of the Alberta Rules of Court in seeking relief. Unless otherwise provided by statute, that Rule permits the court hearing the application for judicial review, to stay the operation of the decision sought to be set aside pending final determination of the review. That Rule does not permit a further application de novo before a single judge of this court. This court does not have jurisdiction to stay the Board's decision in judicial review proceedings. Counsel for the applicants properly interpreted paragraph F (5) of the Consolidated Court of Appeal Practice Directions, to permit applications for a stay to be heard by a single judge. But a stay of an order refusing a stay is a hollow remedy. What the applicants really seek is a reversal of the stays, which are tantamount to an appeal of those decisions. Although the refusal of the stay, may be the subject of an appeal to this court, those appeals must be heard by a panel consisting of a quorum of judges. . . . . . The present applications for a stay of a refusal of a stay are similar in that they amount to a rehearing of the interlocutory stay applications or sitting on an appeal of them, neither of which I have jurisdiction to preside over, sitting as a single judge of this Court. 2. Test for a stay under the Rule In Fawcett v. College of Physicians and Surgeons of the Province of Alberta, 2019 ABQB 788, 2019 CarswellAlta 2133, Justice Little said: [7] The parties agree that pursuant to authorities including Johnston v Alberta (Director of Vital Statistics), 2007 ABCA 394 and Sobeys West Inc. v Alberta College of Pharmacists, 2014 ABQB 333, the test for a stay under Rule 3.23 is the same as for an interlocutory injunction as set out in RJR-MacDonald v Canada (Attorney General) and which may be summarized as follows: 1. Whether there is a serious issue to be tried. 2. Whether the applicant would suffer irreparable harm if the application were refused. 3. Whether the balance of convenience favours the applicant. 3. This Rule only addresses staying the operation of the actual order or decision This Rule allows the reviewing Court to enter a stay of the operation of the actual order or decision which is sought to be set aside through the judicial review. The Rule does not address the ability of the Court whose decision is the subject of the judicial review to continue with the proceedings before that Court. That Court's jurisdiction in relation to those proceedings is suspended by operation of law (see the annotation under Rule 3.15: “Service of notice of the application suspends proceedings in the Alberta Court of Justice”).
